question.:question/problem:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is inconsistent:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=-3 \\ -2x+ky &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & k & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & k & 7\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & k-4 & 1\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=-3 \\ (k-4)y &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The system is inconsistent if it has no solutions. For the system to have no solutions, one of the equations above must be false.

If $k=4,$ then the second equation is $0=1,$ which is false, and the system will have no solution.

Therefore, our system is inconsistent when $k=4.$

question.:question/problem:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x+5y &=-9 \\ x+ky &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-3 & 5 & -9 \\ 1 & k & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-3 & 5 & -9 \\ 1 & k & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & k & 3 \\ -3 & 5 & -9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & k & 3 \\ 0 & 3k+5 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+ky &=3 \\ (3k+5)y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=-\frac{5}{3},$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$, and we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $x+ky=3.$ 

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=-\frac{5}{3}.$
